lessons.title: Present your evidence
lessons.subtitle: Week 16: Demonstration and next steps
lessons.body:
A useful presentation shows the task, artifact, evaluation, improvements, and limitations. Separate demonstrated results from future possibilities.

Offline practice: Prepare a two-minute explanation or a one-page written presentation of your project. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A useful presentation shows the task, artifact, evaluation, improvements, and limitations. Separate demonstrated results from future possibilities.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: UNESCO guidance on responsible AI in education

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains “Present your evidence”?
options: A useful presentation shows the task, artifact, evaluation, improvements, and limitations. Separate demonstrated results from future possibilities.
A polished AI answer is enough evidence that every claim is correct.
The human learner never needs to check the result.
Every task requires training a new model.
questions.explanation: A useful presentation shows the task, artifact, evaluation, improvements, and limitations. Separate demonstrated results from future possibilities.

questions.prompt: For the activity “Prepare a two-minute explanation or a one-page written presentation of your project.”, which approach demonstrates learning?
options: Complete the activity, explain your reasoning, and record a limitation.
Share someone else’s private information to make the example realistic.
Treat an unverified generated response as final evidence.
Skip the activity and copy an unrelated answer.
questions.explanation: The activity asks you to apply this lesson. A written explanation and limitation make your understanding reviewable; a copied result alone does not.

questions.prompt: You return to the “Present your evidence” lesson after a break without internet. What can you do next?
options: Recall the key idea, check saved notes, and complete the offline activity.
Assume a cloud assistant will respond without a connection.
Wait until you can buy a paid AI subscription.
Delete your previous work and start the whole course again.
questions.explanation: The lesson and practice do not require an online tool. Retrieval and a small saved activity help you resume.

lessons.title: Build a portable portfolio
lessons.subtitle: Week 16: Demonstration and next steps
lessons.body:
A portable portfolio can contain a PDF or text artifact, a rubric, a source list, and a reflection. Remove private data before sharing copies.

Offline practice: Organise your final files and write a short index so another person can understand them offline. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

lessons.title: Choose a learning pathway
lessons.subtitle: Week 16: Demonstration and next steps
lessons.body:
Choose next learning based on your goal and prerequisites. Tool use, data literacy, and programming are different paths; verify current course or opportunity details before committing.

Offline practice: Select one next skill and write a plan for checking relevant courses, costs, eligibility, and access. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

lessons.title: Final course demonstration
lessons.subtitle: Week 16: Demonstration and next steps
lessons.body:
Completion means showing what you can explain and apply. Present a reviewed artifact, evidence of corrections, an offline fallback, and a realistic next-step plan.

Offline practice: Final task: recap an AI limitation; practice with your artifact; plan how to verify claims; demonstrate an improvement and explain its evidence. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: Completion means showing what you can explain and apply. Present a reviewed artifact, evidence of corrections, an offline fallback, and a realistic next-step plan.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
